summary: Case case-002 (prof.kaya@aegean.edu) assessed as benign (confidence 0.75). No verified finding IDs (F1…) survive; all three claims were rejected by the Critic. Impossible travel Manisa→Lisbon in 32 min was a non-interactive Exchange sync token, while Lisbon sign-ins used university VPN from known device LT-3104. 193.140.10.21 failures against 54 accounts were shared egress background noise, with 201 distinct MFA successes from the same IP in 30 days. VPN appliance vpn-edge-02 firmware 22.7R2.8 already patches the cited CISA KEV CVEs. No compromise signals survived.

rejected_claims.claim: Impossible travel: Manisa → Lisbon in 32 min
rejected_claims.reason: critic: premature impossible-travel claim: the TR event is a non-interactive mail-sync token (ExchangeSync/15), not the person; the PT sign-ins use university VPN vpn-edge-02 from device LT-3104

rejected_claims.claim: Password spray then success: 193.140.10.21 failed against 54 accounts (60 failures) and later signed in as this user
rejected_claims.reason: critic: 193.140.10.21 looks like shared egress: 201 distinct accounts completed MFA from this IP in the last 30 days (threshold 10); failures across many accounts are expected background noise, not a coordinated spray

rejected_claims.claim: VPN appliance vpn-edge-02 (firmware 22.7R2.8) runs a product listed in CISA KEV (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282, …)
rejected_claims.reason: critic: firmware 22.7R2.8 already includes the fixes for the KEV entries we can version-check (CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282)

actions.action: Close case as benign and document Critic rejection rationale for impossible travel, password spray, and KEV firmware claims.
Maintain standard monitoring for vpn-edge-02 and Exchange non-interactive sync tokens; alert only on interactive sign-ins from new or unknown devices.
If future alerts occur, verify user travel calendar and EDR telemetry for device LT-3104 before escalating.

limitations: Planner model degraded; investigation proceeded with coverage queries only.
earlier model step was degraded; deterministic policy stood in on a complete chain, confidence lowered by 0.1.

- User travel calendar / HR records could not be checked to confirm physical presence in Lisbon.
- Full EDR telemetry for device LT-3104 was not available in this review.
- Independent vulnerability validation of vpn-edge-02 was limited to the vendor version-check claim; no scan was performed.

- Travel calendar for prof.kaya@aegean.edu
- EDR telemetry on LT-3104

- Independent CVE verification on vpn-edge-02 beyond firmware version

risk.rationale: All three initially suspicious signals for prof.kaya@aegean.edu were rejected with reasoned criticism and no surviving verified findings remain. The impossible-travel claim was dismissed because the Turkey event was a non-interactive mail-sync token while Portugal sign-ins used the university VPN from device LT-3104. The password-spray claim was dismissed because 193.140.10.21 is shared egress with 201 distinct MFA completions in 30 days (above the threshold of 10), making failures expected background noise. The VPN appliance CVE exposure was dismissed because firmware 22.7R2.8 already includes fixes for the cited KEV entries. There are no data-quality conflicts and no weak unexplained signals, so this is suspicious signals explained away rather than confirmed takeover, monitoring, or escalation.
